content_of_post_to_comment: ‘Walkabillty’ discourse among urbanist-leaning Americans is funny because it gets so fundamentalist. If you go on certain subreddits and say you have a perfectly walkable life in the United States despite not living in a tier-one city, the Walkability Police will gather to tell you—despite never having been to where you live—that no, you don’t. Then they’ll tell you only Manhattanites and Brooklynites have the ‘quality of life’ of any random person in the Netherlands or France. I’m of course all for maximal walkability, since I do walk most places, and we have so much to learn from Europe and East Asia, but some calming down is at times in order
comment: A useful distinction is between walkability as a daily necessity and walkability as an urban ideal. A small town can offer a walkable routine without having the density, transit, or street life that urbanists are really arguing for.
